questions.explanation: 第一段提到“At first, I thought it would be easy. But soon I felt worried.” 因为挑战是不使用社交媒体，他习惯睡前看手机，所以担心做不到，即挑战太难。B、C、D项文中均未提及。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "detox" in the title probably mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A way to clean the body.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A break from something.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A new phone app.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A kind of food.

questions.explanation: 标题“My Digital Detox Weekend”结合文章内容，作者周末不使用社交媒体，即“数字排毒”，指暂时远离某事物。A项是字面意思，但文中指远离社交媒体；C、D项与文章无关。

title: The Power of the Sun in Our Town
titleZh: 我们镇上的太阳能
passage:
Ten years ago, our town had a big problem. The old power station used coal. It made the air dirty. Many people coughed in winter. The town needed clean energy.

In 2015, the town built a solar farm on the hill. It has many black panels. They catch sunlight and turn it into electricity. Now the farm gives power to over 2,000 homes. The air is much cleaner.

Lily is a middle school student. Her family uses solar power. "We have a small panel on our roof," she says. "It heats water for us. We save money, and we help the Earth."

Solar power is not perfect. It does not work well on cloudy days. But the town also uses wind power. Together, they make our town green.

Lily's teacher, Mr. Wang, says, "Clean energy is the future. Everyone can do something. Turn off the lights when you leave a room. Ride a bike to school. Small actions make a big difference."

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coal is the best energy for towns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Our town uses clean energy to make the air better.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lily's family saves money by using solar power.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wind power is better than solar power.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述小镇过去用煤发电污染空气，后来改用太阳能和风能等清洁能源，使空气更干净。B概括了全文主旨。A与原文相反；C只是文中一个细节；D文中未比较两者优劣。

questions.question: What did the old power station use to make electricity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sunlight

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wind

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water

questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确提到“The old power station used coal.”，所以答案是C。A、B、D都是现在或文中提到的其他能源，但不是旧电站使用的能源。

questions.question: What can we infer about the solar farm from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It works well on cloudy days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It was built on the hill in 2015.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It gives power to less than 2,000 homes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It makes the air dirty.

questions.explanation: 根据第二段“In 2015, the town built a solar farm on the hill.”可知B正确。A与第四段“It does not work well on cloudy days.”矛盾；C与“gives power to over 2,000 homes”矛盾；D与“The air is much cleaner.”矛盾。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "panels" mean in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Large boards that catch sunlight

choices.label: B
choices.text: Small machines that make wind

choices.label: C
choices.text: Old buildings that use coal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Green plants on the hill

questions.explanation: 根据第二段“It has many black panels. They catch sunlight and turn it into electricity.”可知panels是捕捉阳光的黑色板子，即太阳能电池板，所以选A。B、C、D均与上下文不符。

title: The Boy Who Found a Roman Treasure
titleZh: 发现罗马宝藏的男孩
passage:
One sunny morning, 12-year-old Jack was walking on a farm with his father. Suddenly, he saw something shiny in the dirt. He picked it up and found it was a small gold coin.

Jack's father called a museum. Soon, some archaeologists came to the farm. They were very excited. They dug the ground and found over 200 old coins. The coins were from the Roman times, about 2,000 years ago.

"These coins are very important," said Dr. Green, a famous archaeologist. "They tell us how people lived and traded long ago. Jack's careful eyes helped us a lot."

The museum gave Jack a small reward and a certificate. Jack was happy, but he said, "I just wanted to know what it was. I never thought it would be so important."

Now Jack visits the museum often. He says he wants to be an archaeologist when he grows up. "History is like a big puzzle," he says. "Every coin is a piece of it. I want to find more pieces."

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How to become an archaeologist.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A boy's discovery of ancient coins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The history of Roman coins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A trip to a museum.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述了男孩Jack发现古罗马硬币的故事，所以主旨是B。A项文章只是提到Jack想成为考古学家，但这不是主要内容；C项文章没有详细介绍罗马硬币的历史；D项博物馆只是故事的一部分。

questions.question: How many old coins did the archaeologists find?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Twelve.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Over 200.

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 2,000.

questions.explanation: 根据第二段“They dug the ground and found over 200 old coins.”可知，考古学家发现了200多枚硬币，所以选C。A项是Jack最初发现的一枚；B项是Jack的年龄；D项是硬币的年代，不是数量。

questions.question: What can we infer about Jack from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He is afraid of archaeologists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He wants to sell the coins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He is interested in history.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He often visits the farm.

questions.explanation: 根据最后一段Jack说“History is like a big puzzle... I want to find more pieces.”以及他经常去博物馆，想成为考古学家，可以推断他对历史感兴趣，所以选C。A项文章未提及；B项文章说博物馆给了他奖励，没说他想卖硬币；D项文章只提到他经常去博物馆，不是农场。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "reward" in Paragraph 4 probably mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A sum of money given for finding something.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A letter of thanks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A book about history.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A job in the museum.

questions.explanation: 根据上下文，博物馆因为Jack的发现给了他“reward”和一张证书，可以推测“reward”是“报酬、奖金”的意思，所以选A。B项证书是certificate，不是reward；C项和D项文章未提及。

title: My Secret to Learning English
titleZh: 我学英语的秘密
passage:
Last year, English was a big problem for me. I could not remember new words. I was afraid to speak in class. My teacher, Ms. Li, gave me some advice. She said, "Don't just read. Use the words."

So I started a small notebook. Every day, I wrote down five new words. Then I made a short sentence with each word. At first, it was slow. But after two weeks, I could do it faster. I also joined an English club. We met every Friday. We played games and talked about our hobbies. I felt shy at first. But my friends were kind. They helped me a lot.

Now I love English. I can speak in class. I can also read easy English storybooks. Learning a language is like making a cake. You need time, practice, and a little love. If you are patient, you will get a sweet result.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How to make a cake.

choices.label: B
choices.text: How the writer learned English.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Why English is difficult.

choices.label: D
choices.text: How to join an English club.

questions.explanation: 文章讲述了作者从害怕英语到喜欢英语的过程，重点介绍了他学习英语的方法，因此B是主旨。A只是文中的一个比喻；C只是第一段提到的问题，不是全文重点；D只是学习英语的一个具体做法，不全面。

questions.question: What did the writer do every day after Ms. Li's advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He read English storybooks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He talked with his friends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He wrote down five new words and made sentences.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He played games in class.

questions.explanation: 第二段第二、三句明确说“Every day, I wrote down five new words. Then I made a short sentence with each word.”所以C正确。A是现在能做的事；B是参加俱乐部时做的事；D是俱乐部里的活动，不是每天做的事。

questions.question: How did the writer feel at the English club at first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excited.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Angry.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bored.

questions.explanation: 第二段倒数第三句说“I felt shy at first.”，所以B正确。其他选项文中没有提到。

questions.question: What does the writer compare learning a language to?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Making a cake.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Playing a game.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reading a book.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Writing a notebook.

questions.explanation: 最后一段第三句说“Learning a language is like making a cake.”，所以A正确。B、C、D虽然文中提到过，但不是作者用来比喻语言学习的。

title: The School Music Club
titleZh: 学校音乐俱乐部
passage:
Kate loves music. She sings every day. But she is shy. She never sings in front of others.

One day, Kate sees a notice at school. It says: "Join the Music Club! We meet every Friday." Kate wants to join. But she is afraid.

Her friend Lucy says, "Come with me. You can just listen first." Kate goes to the club. There are ten students. Some play the guitar. Some sing.

A boy named Tom plays the piano. The music is beautiful. Kate smiles. She starts to sing quietly. Lucy hears her and says, "Your voice is great!" Kate's face turns red. But she feels happy.

Now Kate goes to the club every Friday. She sings with her friends. She is not shy anymore. Music brings her joy and new friends.

Last week, the club gave a show. Kate sang a song. Everyone clapped. Kate's mother said, "I am proud of you." Kate smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love music."

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Kate learns to play the piano.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Kate changes from shy to confident through music.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The school has many clubs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lucy is a good singer.

questions.explanation: 全文讲述 Kate 从害羞不敢唱歌，到加入音乐俱乐部后变得自信并享受音乐，因此 B 正确。A 错误，因为 Kate 是唱歌，不是学钢琴；C 太泛，文章只讲了音乐俱乐部；D 错误，Lucy 是鼓励 Kate 的人，但文章没有说她唱歌好。

questions.question: How does Kate feel at first when she goes to the club?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Angry

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excited

choices.label: C
choices.text: Afraid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bored

questions.explanation: 文章第二段说 Kate wants to join. But she is afraid. 因此她一开始是害怕的，C 正确。A 生气、B 兴奋、D 无聊都不符合原文。

questions.question: What can we infer about Kate from the last paragraph?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She still feels shy now.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She doesn't like the club.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She is proud of her mother.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She enjoys singing for others now.

questions.explanation: 最后一段说 Kate 在表演中唱歌，大家都鼓掌，她说 I love music，说明她现在享受为别人唱歌，D 正确。A 错误，文中已说她 not shy anymore；B 错误，她每周都去俱乐部；C 错误，是妈妈为她骄傲，不是她为妈妈骄傲。

questions.question: What does the word "clapped" mean in the last paragraph?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stood up

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sang songs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hit hands together to show praise

choices.label: D
choices.text: Left the room

questions.explanation: 根据上下文，Kate 唱完歌后，大家 clapped，这是表示赞赏的动作，因此 clapped 意为“鼓掌”，C 正确。A 站起来、B 唱歌、D 离开房间都不符合语境。

title: Riding to School Together
titleZh: 一起骑车上学
passage:
Li Ming and his father live in a small town. Li Ming's school is about three kilometers from home. In the past, his father drove him to school every day. The car ride took about fifteen minutes.

Last month, his father bought two new bikes. Now they ride to school together every morning. They leave home at seven o'clock. The bike ride takes about twenty minutes. It is a little slower, but Li Ming likes it much better.

On the way, they pass a park and a small river. They can see birds, trees and flowers. Sometimes they meet Li Ming's classmates. They say hello and ride together. Li Ming feels happy and relaxed. He is ready for a new school day.

"Riding is good for us," his father says. "It is good for the air, too." Li Ming agrees. He also thinks it is a good way to talk with his father. They talk about school, friends and sports. These twenty minutes are their special time.

Now more families in the town ride bikes. Li Ming hopes more people will join them. It is good for their health and the environment.

questions.question: What is the best title for this passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A Small Town and Its Parks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Riding Bikes to School

choices.label: C
choices.text: How to Buy a Good Bike

choices.label: D
choices.text: Li Ming's Favorite Sport

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲李明和爸爸从开车上学改为一起骑车上学，以及骑车带来的好处，所以最佳标题是B。A只提到了小镇和公园，太片面；C文章没有讲如何买自行车；D文章的主题不是运动，而是交通出行方式的变化。

questions.question: How long does the bike ride take?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About five minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: About fifteen minutes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: About twenty minutes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: About thirty minutes.

questions.explanation: 文中明确说“The bike ride takes about twenty minutes.”，所以选C。A、B、D文中都没有提到，其中B是过去开车上学的时间，不能混淆。

questions.question: What can we learn from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Li Ming's school is very far from his home.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Li Ming's father doesn't like driving a car.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Li Ming and his father enjoy their time together.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Li Ming's classmates also ride bikes to school.

questions.explanation: 文章说李明觉得骑车更开心、更放松，还说这二十分钟是他和爸爸的特殊时间，可以推断他们很享受在一起的时光，所以选C。A错，学校离家约三公里，不算很远；B文中没有说爸爸不喜欢开车；D文中只说有时会遇到同学，并没有说同学也骑车上学。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "join" mean in the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: become a member of a group

choices.label: B
choices.text: take part in an activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: help other people

choices.label: D
choices.text: buy something new

questions.explanation: 根据上下文“Li Ming hopes more people will join them.”，join them 指加入他们一起骑车的活动，所以选B“参加一项活动”。A“成为团体成员”不符合这里的情境；C“帮助别人”和D“买新东西”都与上下文意思不符。

title: The Saturday Helper
titleZh: 周六小帮手
passage:
Li Hua is a middle school student. He likes helping others. Every Saturday morning, he goes to the Old People's Home near his school. He helps the old people there.

At the Old People's Home, Li Hua does many things. He cleans the windows and waters the flowers. He also reads newspapers to the old people. Sometimes he plays chess with them. The old people are very happy to see him. They call him "our little helper".

Last Saturday, Li Hua met an old man named Mr. Wang. Mr. Wang was sad because his son lived far away. Li Hua sat with him and talked for a long time. Mr. Wang smiled at last. "You are like my grandson," he said. Li Hua felt very happy.

Li Hua's parents are proud of him. His teacher says he is a good example for other students. Li Hua says, "Helping others is not hard. It just takes a little time and love. I will keep doing it."

Now Li Hua wants more classmates to join him. Next Saturday, three friends will go with him. They will sing songs and tell stories to the old people. Li Hua hopes everyone can find a way to help others.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An old man's sad life.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A student's volunteer work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: How to play chess well.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A school singing activity.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲中学生李华每周六去敬老院做志愿服务，并带动同学一起参与，故选 B。A 只涉及文中一个细节（王爷爷），不是全文主旨；C 文中只提到下棋，不是主题；D 唱歌只是最后一段提到的未来活动，不能概括全文。

questions.question: What does Li Hua do at the Old People's Home?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He cooks meals for the old people.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He cleans windows and reads newspapers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He takes the old people to his school.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He helps the old people find their sons.

questions.explanation: 第二段明确写到李华擦窗户、浇花、给老人读报纸、下棋，故选 B。A 文中没有提到做饭；C 文中没有提到带老人去学校；D 文中只说王爷爷的儿子住得远，李华并没有帮老人找儿子。

questions.question: Why did Mr. Wang smile at last?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because his son came to see him.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Because Li Hua talked with him.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because he won a chess game.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because he got a new grandson.

questions.explanation: 第三段说王爷爷因为儿子住得远而难过，李华坐下来和他聊了很久，最后王爷爷笑了，可推断是因为李华的陪伴让他开心，故选 B。A 文中没有说儿子来了；C 文中没有提到下棋输赢；D 王爷爷只是说李华像他的孙子，并不是真的有了新孙子。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "proud" in Paragraph 4 mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feeling happy about someone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Feeling worried about someone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Feeling angry with someone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Feeling sorry for someone.

questions.explanation: 第四段说李华的爸爸妈妈为他感到 proud，老师也说他是个好榜样，说明父母因他而高兴、自豪，故 proud 意为“为某人感到高兴/自豪”，选 A。B 担心、C 生气、D 同情都不符合语境。

title: The Little Money Jar
titleZh: 小存钱罐
passage:
Lily is a 13-year-old girl. She gets 20 yuan from her parents every week. Last month, she saw a nice schoolbag in a shop. It cost 100 yuan. She really wanted it.

But Lily had a problem. She spent all her money on snacks and small toys. She had only 10 yuan in her money jar. "I can't buy the bag now," she thought. "I need to save money."

So Lily made a plan. She decided to save 10 yuan every week. She stopped buying snacks after school. She also brought water from home instead of buying drinks. Her friend Lucy asked, "Why don't you buy ice cream with us?" Lily smiled and said, "I'm saving for something special."

Five weeks later, Lily had 60 yuan. Her parents were happy to see her change. They gave her 40 yuan as a gift. Now she had 100 yuan! She ran to the shop and bought the schoolbag.

Lily learned an important lesson. Saving a little money each week can help you get what you want. Now she still saves money. She wants to buy a new book next month.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lily's parents give her 20 yuan every week.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Saving money little by little helps you buy what you want.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schoolbags are very expensive for students.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lily likes to eat snacks after school.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述Lily通过每周存钱最终买到书包的故事，说明积少成多可以实现目标。A、C、D都是文章中的细节，不是主旨。

questions.question: How much money did Lily have in her money jar at first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 20 yuan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 10 yuan.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 60 yuan.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 100 yuan.

questions.explanation: 文章第二段明确提到“She had only 10 yuan in her money jar.”，所以最初有10元。A是每周得到的钱，C是五周后存的钱，D是书包的价格。

questions.question: What can we infer about Lily from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She doesn't like ice cream.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She will stop saving money soon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She becomes better at managing money.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She asks her parents for more money every week.

questions.explanation: 从Lily制定存钱计划、停止买零食、带水上学等行为可以推断她学会了管理自己的钱。A文中未说她不喜欢冰淇淋；B与最后一段“Now she still saves money”矛盾；D文中没有提到。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "special" in Paragraph 3 mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Very cheap.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Very important or dear to her.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Very easy to get.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Very strange.

questions.explanation: 根据上下文，Lily存钱是为了买她非常想要的书包，所以“special”在这里指“对她来说很重要或很珍贵的”。A、C、D都不符合语境。

title: The Little Invention That Helps Grandma
titleZh: 帮助奶奶的小发明
topic: 科技与发明——为奶奶设计提醒药盒
passage:
Li Wei is a 13-year-old boy from a small town. He lives with his grandma. She is 75 years old. Every day, she needs to take three kinds of pills. But she often forgets.

One evening, Li Wei saw his grandma looking for her pills everywhere. She looked worried. "I can't remember if I took them," she said. Li Wei felt sad. He wanted to help her.

The next day, he had an idea. He found a small box and some colored stickers at home. He put red stickers on the box for morning pills. Blue stickers were for noon. Green stickers were for night. He also drew a big sun and a moon on the box.

Then he asked his father for help. They put a small clock inside the box. At 7 a.m., 12 p.m., and 7 p.m., the clock rings. The sound is soft, like a bird singing. When Grandma hears it, she opens the box and takes the right pills.

Now Grandma doesn't forget her pills. She says, "My grandson's gift is better than any expensive machine." Li Wei smiles. He knows that a good invention doesn't need to be big or costly. It just needs to solve a real problem with love.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Li Wei's grandma is very old and forgetful.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Li Wei made a simple invention to help his grandma.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Li Wei's father is good at making machines.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Expensive machines are better than simple gifts.

questions.explanation: 主旨题。全文讲述李伟为健忘的奶奶发明了一个带闹钟和贴纸的药盒，帮助她按时吃药。B项概括了核心事件。A项只是背景细节，C项文中未提，D项与文意相反。

questions.question: Why did Li Wei decide to make the box?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He wanted to win a school science prize.

choices.label: B
choices.text: His father asked him to do it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He saw his grandma worried about forgetting her pills.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 细节题。第二段描述李伟看到奶奶到处找药、担心忘记是否吃过药，于是决定帮忙。C项与此一致。A、B、D项文中均未提及。

questions.question: What can we infer about Li Wei from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He is creative and cares about his family.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He is good at math and science.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He often forgets things too.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He doesn't like expensive machines.

questions.explanation: 推理题。李伟观察到奶奶的困难后，主动用贴纸、时钟等简单材料制作提醒药盒，体现了他有创意和关心家人。B项文中未提，C项无依据，D项不能从文中推出。

questions.question: What does the word "costly" in the last paragraph mean?

title: The Three R's at Maple Leaf Middle School
titleZh: 枫叶中学的环保三原则
topic: 环境保护（校园环保行动）
passage:
Maple Leaf Middle School started a "Green Week" last Monday. The goal was simple: reduce, reuse, and recycle. Every class had to find ways to help the environment.

In Class 8, students noticed a big problem. Their classroom had two large trash bins. One was for paper, and the other was for other waste. But many students threw paper cups into the wrong bin. So the class made colorful signs. The signs said, "Paper here!" and "Other waste here!" They also put small boxes on each desk for used paper.

After one week, the class collected 15 kilograms of paper. They sold it to a recycling center and got 30 yuan. With the money, they bought two small plants for the classroom.

"We learned that small actions can make a big difference," said Li Hua, a student in Class 8. "Now we always think before we throw things away."

The school hopes to have more Green Weeks in the future. Next time, they plan to ask students to bring reusable water bottles and lunch boxes.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maple Leaf Middle School has a new recycling center.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Class 8 students made signs to decorate their classroom.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A school's Green Week helped students learn to protect the environment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Students sold paper to buy plants for their school.

questions.explanation: 文章讲述了枫叶中学举办‘绿色周’活动，学生学会减少浪费、回收利用，并意识到小行动也能保护环境，因此C是主旨。A错误，文中只说把纸卖给回收中心，不是学校有回收中心；B是细节，不是主旨；D是活动中的一个具体例子，不是全文主旨。

questions.question: What problem did Class 8 students notice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There were not enough trash bins in the classroom.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students put paper cups into the wrong bin.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The classroom had no signs on the walls.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The recycling center was too far away.

questions.explanation: 文章第二段提到‘many students threw paper cups into the wrong bin’，即学生把纸杯扔错了垃圾桶，所以B正确。A错误，教室有两个大垃圾桶，不是不够；C错误，没有标志是问题，但他们自己做了标志；D文中未提到回收中心很远。

questions.question: What can we infer from the passage about Li Hua?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He doesn't like the Green Week.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He thinks small actions are not useful.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He will be more careful about throwing things away.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He wants to sell more paper to buy plants.

questions.explanation: 李华说‘Now we always think before we throw things away’，说明他以后扔东西前会思考，会更加小心，因此C正确。A错误，他积极参与并学到东西；B错误，他说小行动能带来大改变；D错误，买植物是班级行为，不是他的个人目标。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "reuse" in Paragraph 1 probably mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use something again

choices.label: B
choices.text: Throw something away

choices.label: C
choices.text: Buy something new

choices.label: D
choices.text: Make something beautiful

questions.explanation: 根据第一段‘reduce, reuse, and recycle’以及后文提到带可重复使用的水瓶和饭盒，可以推断reuse意为‘再次使用’，所以A正确。B‘扔掉’、C‘买新的’、D‘使美丽’都不符合语境。

title: A Family Walk That Changed Us
titleZh: 一次改变我们的家庭散步
passage:
Last year, my family was not very healthy. My father worked all day and sat in a chair for hours. My mother liked watching TV after dinner. My brother and I played computer games in our free time. We seldom did sports, and we often felt tired.

One evening, my father said, "Let's take a walk after dinner." We were surprised, but we agreed. That first walk was short—only twenty minutes. We walked slowly and talked about our day. It was relaxing.

We decided to walk every evening. At first, it was hard. Sometimes we wanted to stay at home. But we kept going. After a month, we could walk for an hour. We felt stronger and happier. My father lost some weight. My mother stopped watching TV so much. My brother and I spent less time on games.

Now we also ride bikes on weekends. We go to the park and enjoy the fresh air. We are not a sports family, but we are a walking family. Exercise is now part of our life. It brings us good health and makes us closer.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Watching TV is bad for health.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A family changed their life by exercising together.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children should not play computer games.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Walking is better than riding bikes.

questions.explanation: 文章讲述了作者一家通过每天散步、周末骑车，变得健康和亲密。B项准确概括了全文。A、C只涉及文中细节，不是主旨；D项文中并未比较散步和骑车。

questions.question: What did the family do after dinner one evening?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They watched TV together.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They played computer games.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They took a short walk.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They rode bikes in the park.

questions.explanation: 根据第二段，一天晚饭后父亲提议散步，他们走了一小段路（only twenty minutes）。C项正确。A、B是之前的行为；D是后来周末的活动。

questions.question: What can we infer about the family from the last paragraph?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They will stop walking soon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They only exercise on weekends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They enjoy spending time together.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They want to become sports stars.

questions.explanation: 最后一段提到“makes us closer”，说明他们享受在一起的时光。A与文意相反；B与“walk every evening”矛盾；D文中未提及。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "relaxing" in Paragraph 2 mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Making people feel calm and happy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Making people feel tired.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Making people feel worried.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Making people feel hungry.

questions.explanation: 根据第二段“We walked slowly and talked about our day. It was relaxing.”可知，散步让他们感到放松、平静和愉快。A项正确。B、C、D均不符合语境。

title: The New Class Newspaper
titleZh: 班级新报纸
passage:
Ms. Li teaches English at a middle school. Last month, she gave her class a new task. The students would make a class newspaper in English. Many students felt worried. They thought it was too hard.

Ms. Li did not give them a test. She did not ask them to remember long texts. Instead, she put the students into six groups. Each group had four students. Every group chose one topic. Some chose school sports. Some chose pets. One group chose how to save water.

At first, the students made many mistakes. But Ms. Li did not correct every mistake for them. She asked them to read their own writing again. Then they helped each other in the group. Slowly, their English became better and better.

After three weeks, the newspaper was ready. It had ten pages. There were stories, small pictures, and even a short poem. The students were very happy. They read it again and again.

Tom, a quiet boy, said, "I was afraid at first. But now I like English more." Ms. Li smiled and said, "You learn best when you use the language, not just remember it."

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Why students dislike English tests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: How a teacher helped students learn by making a newspaper.

choices.label: C
choices.text: How to make a class newspaper in three weeks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Why school sports are popular in middle school.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述李老师通过让学生制作英文班报来学习英语，而不是通过考试或背诵，故选B。A项文中没有说学生讨厌考试；C项只是文章的一部分，不是主旨；D项只是其中一个小组的话题，太片面。

questions.question: How did Ms. Li help her students with their mistakes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She corrected every mistake for them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: She asked them to take a test.

choices.label: C
choices.text: She let them read their writing again and help each other.

choices.label: D
choices.text: She wrote the newspaper for them.

questions.explanation: 文中第三段提到，李老师没有替学生改正每一个错误，而是让他们再读自己的文章，并在小组内互相帮助，故选C。A项与原文相反；B项文中没有提到考试；D项文中说学生自己完成报纸，不是老师代写。

questions.question: What can we infer (推断) about Tom from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He was good at English before.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He did not join the newspaper task.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He becomes more interested in English now.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He still feels afraid of English.

questions.explanation: 文章最后一段Tom说“一开始我很害怕，但现在我更喜欢英语了”，可以推断他现在对英语更感兴趣了，故选C。A项与“一开始害怕”不符；B项文中说他是参与者；D项与“现在更喜欢”矛盾。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "correct" in Paragraph 3 mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To make right

choices.label: B
choices.text: To read aloud

choices.label: C
choices.text: To write down

choices.label: D
choices.text: To talk about

questions.explanation: 根据第三段“But Ms. Li did not correct every mistake for them. She asked them to read their own writing again.”可知，这里correct指“改正、纠正错误”，即“make right”，故选A。B项“大声读”、C项“写下”、D项“谈论”都不符合语境。

title: The Helpful Robot in Our Classroom
titleZh: 我们教室里乐于助人的机器人
passage:
Last month, a small robot came to our classroom. Its name is Robo. It is about one meter tall. It has a screen for a face and two bright blue eyes. Our teacher told us that Robo is a robot with AI, which means it can learn and help us.

Robo helps us in many ways. In the morning, it says hello to everyone and checks our homework. If we make a mistake, it shows us the right answer on its screen. In class, it can answer our questions. For example, when we ask about a math problem, it explains it step by step. It never gets angry, even if we ask the same question many times.

However, Robo is not perfect. It cannot understand jokes, and it sometimes gives wrong answers. Last week, it said the sun goes around the earth. We all laughed. Our teacher said AI is smart but not perfect. It still needs people to help it.

I like Robo. It makes learning fun. But I also know that AI is a tool. It can help us, but it cannot take the place of our teachers. We should use it wisely.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Robo is a robot that can do everything.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AI robots like Robo can help us but are not perfect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Robo is better than our teachers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: We should not use AI in school.

questions.explanation: 文章主要介绍了教室里的AI机器人Robo能帮助学生学习，但也有不完美之处，最后指出AI是工具，需要明智使用。A项说它能做一切，与原文不符；C项说它比老师更好，原文明确说不能取代老师；D项说我们不应该在学校使用AI，与作者态度相反。因此B正确。

questions.question: What can Robo do in the classroom?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can tell jokes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can check homework and answer questions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It can teach all subjects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can take the place of teachers.

questions.explanation: 根据第二段，Robo可以在早上检查作业，在课堂上回答问题。A项说它会讲笑话，原文说它不懂笑话；C项说它能教所有科目，未提及；D项说它能取代老师，原文明确说不能。因此B正确。

questions.question: What can we infer from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Robo is a perfect robot.

choices.label: B
choices.text: AI can make mistakes sometimes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Robo can understand jokes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Teachers are not important now.

questions.explanation: 根据第三段，Robo有时会给出错误答案，例如说太阳绕着地球转，这说明AI有时会犯错。A项说它是完美的，与原文矛盾；C项说它能理解笑话，原文说不能；D项说老师不重要，与原文最后一段不符。因此B正确。

questions.question: What does the word "tool" in the last paragraph mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A machine that can think like a human.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Something that helps us do things.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A person who teaches students.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A game that students play.

questions.explanation: 根据最后一段，作者说AI是一个工具，它能帮助我们，但不能取代老师。结合上下文，tool指的是帮助我们做事情的东西。A项是机器能像人一样思考，不准确；C项是老师，不对；D项是游戏，不对。因此B正确。

title: The Cat That Rings the Bell
titleZh: 会按门铃的猫
passage:
Lily has a cat named Mimi. Mimi is three years old. She is white and very smart.

One morning, Lily found Mimi sitting by the door. The doorbell was ringing. But no one was outside. Lily opened the door and looked around. There was no one there. She felt surprised.

A few minutes later, the doorbell rang again. Lily ran to the door quickly. This time, she saw Mimi standing on a small chair. The cat put her paw on the doorbell. It rang! Lily laughed. "Mimi, you are a clever cat!" she said.

Why did Mimi ring the doorbell? Lily thought about it. Mimi liked to go outside in the morning. She wanted Lily to open the door for her. So she learned to use the doorbell.

Lily told her friend Tom about it. Tom didn't believe her. "A cat can't do that!" he said. The next day, Tom came to Lily's house. He sat in the living room. Suddenly, the doorbell rang. Tom opened the door. There was Mimi! Tom was very surprised. "You are right, Lily!" he said. "Your cat is really amazing!"

Now Mimi rings the doorbell every morning. Lily says it is a good way for Mimi to say, "Let me out, please!"

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A clever cat that can ring a doorbell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: How to teach a cat to open a door.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lily and her friend Tom.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Why cats like to go outside.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述了一只名叫咪咪的猫学会按门铃的故事，表现了猫的聪明。A选项正确概括了文章主旨。B选项文章未提到教猫开门；C选项汤姆只是其中一个人物，不是主要内容；D选项文章只提到咪咪喜欢早上出去，并未讨论猫为什么喜欢出去。

questions.question: When did Mimi ring the doorbell for the first time according to the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the morning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the afternoon.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the evening.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At night.

questions.explanation: 文章第一段提到“One morning, Lily found Mimi sitting by the door. The doorbell was ringing.”，说明第一次听到门铃响是在早上。B、C、D选项在文中均未提及。

questions.question: What can we infer from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mimi rings the doorbell to ask Lily to open the door.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tom has a cat at home, too.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lily doesn't like Mimi to go outside.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mimi rings the doorbell every evening.

questions.explanation: 文章第四段提到“Mimi liked to go outside in the morning. She wanted Lily to open the door for her. So she learned to use the doorbell.”，因此可以推断咪咪按门铃是为了让莉莉开门。B选项文中未提到汤姆养猫；C选项莉莉并没有不喜欢咪咪出去；D选项文章最后说“every morning”，不是every evening。

questions.question: What does the word "amazing" in the passage mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Very surprising and clever.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Very lazy and slow.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Very big and strong.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Very common and usual.

questions.explanation: 根据上下文，汤姆看到咪咪按门铃后非常惊讶，并说“Your cat is really amazing!”，说明amazing在这里表示“令人惊奇的、聪明的”。B选项“懒惰缓慢”、C选项“大而强壮”、D选项“普通平常”均不符合语境。

title: A Teenager's Dream of Space
titleZh: 一个少年的太空梦
passage:
Li Wei is a 14-year-old boy from Beijing. He loves space. His room is full of model rockets, space books and posters of astronauts. Every night, he looks at the stars and dreams of becoming an astronaut.

Last month, Li Wei's school held a science week. A real astronaut came to give a talk. Li Wei was very excited. He asked many questions. "What is it like to live in space?" "How do you sleep?" "What do you eat?" The astronaut answered every question with a smile.

After the talk, Li Wei learned something important. Astronauts must be healthy. They must study hard and learn many skills. They also need to work well with others. "I thought space travel was just fun," Li Wei said. "Now I know it needs a lot of hard work."

Li Wei decided to change his habits. He started running every morning. He read more science books. He also joined the school's science club. His teacher says, "Li Wei is working hard for his dream. We all hope he can make it one day."

Li Wei knows it is not easy to become an astronaut. But he will not give up. "The stars are far away," he says. "But if I keep trying, I can get closer."

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How astronauts live in space.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A boy who wants to be an astronaut.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A school science week in Beijing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Why space travel is fun.

questions.explanation: 全文围绕李伟的太空梦想展开，包括他的爱好、听了宇航员的报告后改变习惯并为之努力，故B正确。A是文中提到的细节，不是主旨；C只是故事的一个事件；D与文中“not just fun”的表述相悖。

questions.question: What did Li Wei learn from the astronaut's talk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Astronauts eat very little food.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Astronauts sleep in special beds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Astronauts need to be healthy and learn many skills.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Astronauts do not need to work with others.

questions.explanation: 文中第四段明确提到“Astronauts must be healthy. They must study hard and learn many skills. They also need to work well with others.”，故C正确。A、B文中未提及；D与原文相反。

questions.question: What can we infer about Li Wei from the last paragraph?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He will give up his dream soon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: He is sure to become an astronaut.

choices.label: C
choices.text: He thinks space is too far to reach.

choices.label: D
choices.text: He will keep working hard for his dream.

questions.explanation: 最后一段李伟说“But he will not give up”和“if I keep trying, I can get closer”，说明他会继续努力，故D正确。A与原文相反；B文中未说他一定能成为宇航员；C是他对距离的客观描述，不是他的态度。

questions.question: What does the underlined word "make it" in Paragraph 4 mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrive at a place.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Achieve his dream.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Make a model rocket.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Answer a question.

questions.explanation: 根据上下文，老师说的是“We all hope he can make it one day.”，指的是李伟实现成为宇航员的梦想，故B正确。A、C、D均不符合语境。

title: A Special Lunch at School
titleZh: 学校里的特别午餐
passage:
Last Friday, our school had a special lunch. There was no meat on the menu. All the food was vegetables, fruit and rice. Many students were surprised. "Where is the chicken?" asked Tom.

Miss Li, our science teacher, smiled and said, "Today is No Meat Day. We want to show that healthy meals can be delicious without meat." She told us that eating too much meat is not good for our body. Vegetables and fruit give us vitamins. They help us stay strong and grow well.

At first, some students were not happy. But when they tasted the food, they changed their minds. The tomato soup was sweet. The carrot salad was fresh. Even Tom said, "This is better than I thought!"

After lunch, we had a class meeting. We talked about our eating habits. Many of us eat fast food every week. Some students drink cola every day. We learned that we should eat more vegetables and fruit. We should also drink water instead of sweet drinks.

Now, our class has a small garden. We grow tomatoes and carrots there. We want to eat what we grow. It is fun and healthy. I think good eating habits start from small changes.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students should not eat meat at all.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A school activity helps students learn about healthy eating.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tom likes tomato soup better than chicken.

choices.label: D

title: The Little Garden on the Roof
titleZh: 屋顶上的小花园
passage:
Mr. Lee lives in a tall building in the city. Every morning, he takes the elevator to the 20th floor. But he doesn't go to work. He goes to the roof.

On the roof, there is a small garden. Mr. Lee grows tomatoes, carrots, and flowers there. "I have lived in the city for thirty years," he says. "I love the city, but I also miss the green fields of my hometown. So I made this garden."

Many neighbors visit his garden. They are surprised. "We didn't know a garden could be here!" they say. Mr. Lee gives them fresh vegetables. He also teaches children how to plant seeds.

Now, some other people in the building are starting their own roof gardens. "The city is busy and noisy," Mr. Lee says. "But a little green can make people feel happy and calm."

In big cities, space is limited. But with a little imagination, people can find ways to be close to nature. Mr. Lee's roof garden is a good example.

title: The Kite That Carried Spring
titleZh: 载着春天的风筝
passage:
Every spring, Li Ming's grandfather takes him to the park to fly a kite. But this kite is not a toy from a shop. It is a beautiful swallow kite made of bamboo and paper.

Grandfather says that in China, flying kites is an old tradition. Long ago, people flew kites to welcome spring and wish for good luck. They painted the kites with bright colours and happy pictures. A swallow kite means spring is coming and life is full of hope.

Li Ming wants to learn how to make a kite. So Grandfather teaches him. First, they choose thin bamboo sticks. Then they tie them together to make the shape of a swallow. Next, they cover the frame with paper and paint it black and white. Finally, they tie a long string to the kite.

It takes them three afternoons to finish the kite. When Li Ming flies it for the first time, he feels very proud. The kite dances in the blue sky like a real bird.

"This is not just a kite," says Grandfather. "It carries our family's love and our Chinese culture. One day, you will teach your children to make one, too."

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Li Ming learns to make and fly a traditional Chinese kite with his grandfather.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Swallow kites are the most beautiful kites in the world.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children should play outside more often in spring.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grandfather is very good at making bamboo sticks.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述了李明和爷爷一起制作并放飞传统中国风筝的故事，还提到了风筝背后的文化意义，故 A 正确。B 项“燕子风筝是世界上最美的风筝”只是文中提到燕子风筝漂亮，并非主旨；C 项“孩子春天应多户外活动”不是文章重点；D 项“爷爷很会做竹条”只是制作过程中的一个细节，不是主旨。

questions.explanation: 文章第二段明确提到“Long ago, people flew kites to welcome spring and wish for good luck.”，故 B 正确。A 项“卖钱”文中未提；C 项“和鸟交朋友”无中生有；D 项“练习绘画”文中只是说在风筝上画明亮的颜色和快乐的图案，并非放风筝的目的。

questions.question: What can we infer about Li Ming from the passage?

questions.explanation: 根据第三段“Li Ming wants to learn how to make a kite.”以及他花三个下午认真制作，可推断他对学习传统技艺感兴趣，故 C 正确。A 项“他以前做过很多风筝”文中没有依据；B 项“一开始不喜欢放风筝”与第一段“Every spring, Li Ming's grandfather takes him to the park to fly a kite.”及后文感到自豪矛盾；D 项“他想未来成为风筝制作者”过度推断，文中只说他向爷爷学习制作。

questions.question: What does the word "frame" mean in Paragraph 3?

choices.label: A

title: The Power of a Smile
titleZh: 微笑的力量
topic: 心理学发现——微笑能让人更快乐
passage:
Smiling is not just a way to show you are happy. Scientists have found that it can also make you feel happier. This is called the "facial feedback" effect. When you smile, your brain gets a message from your face. Then it starts to feel good.

In one study, two groups of students watched funny cartoons. One group held a pen in their mouths in a way that made them smile. The other group held the pen in a way that stopped them from smiling. The first group said the cartoons were funnier. Their smiling faces helped them enjoy the cartoons more.

Another study found that smiling can even help you do better in school. When you smile, you feel less worried. Then you can think more clearly and learn new things faster.

But not all smiles work the same. A true smile uses both your mouth and your eyes. A fake smile only uses your mouth. Scientists say true smiles are better for your health and your mood.

So next time you feel sad, try to smile. You may find that your mood changes. It costs nothing, but it can make your day better.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smiling can make people feel happier and do better.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Watching funny cartoons is good for students.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Holding a pen in the mouth is a funny habit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: True smiles are the same as fake smiles.

questions.explanation: 文章主题是微笑能让人更快乐、学习更好。A项概括了全文核心。B项只是研究中的一个例子，不是主旨。C项是实验细节，不是文章重点。D项与原文相反，原文说真笑和假笑不同。

questions.question: In the study, which group said the cartoons were funnier?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The group that held the pen to stop smiling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The group that held the pen to make them smile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both groups said the same.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither group liked the cartoons.

questions.explanation: 原文说 'The first group said the cartoons were funnier. Their smiling faces helped them enjoy the cartoons more.' 第一组用笔让自己微笑，所以觉得卡通更有趣。A项是另一组，C项与原文不符，D项错误。

questions.question: What can we infer from the passage about smiling?

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smiling makes you feel more worried.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 原文提到 'When you smile, you feel less worried. Then you can think more clearly and learn new things faster.' 由此可推断微笑有助于更清晰地思考。B项太绝对，原文说真笑更好，但没说只有真笑有用。C项与原文相反。D项与原文建议相反。

title: A Special Take Your Child to Work Day
titleZh: 特别的带孩子上班日
passage:
Every April, many companies have a special day. It is called "Take Your Child to Work Day". On this day, parents bring their children to their offices. The children can see what their parents do at work.

Last month, it was my turn. My mother works at a small animal hospital. I woke up early and felt very excited. When we arrived, I saw many dogs and cats. Some were sick. Some were just there for a check-up.

My mother is a vet. She showed me how to hold a little dog gently. She also let me watch her give medicine to a cat. I was a bit scared at first, but my mother said, "Don't worry. Just be kind and careful." I tried my best. The cat was quiet and did not move.

At lunch time, we ate sandwiches in the break room. I met other vets and nurses. They told me funny stories about their animal patients. I laughed a lot.

Before we went home, my mother asked, "What do you think of my job?" I thought for a moment and said, "It's hard, but you help animals every day. That's great!" My mother smiled. Now I want to be a vet, too.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children should visit their parents' offices every month.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The writer spent a day at her mother's workplace and learned about her job.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Being a vet is the best job in the world.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Take Your Child to Work Day is only for animal doctors.

questions.explanation: 文章讲述作者在“带孩子上班日”去妈妈工作的动物医院，了解妈妈作为兽医的工作，并深受启发。B 项准确概括了全文主旨。A 项“每月”错误，原文是每年四月；C 项“最好的工作”过于绝对，原文只说“很棒”；D 项“只针对动物医生”错误，原文说许多公司都有这个活动。

title: The Day I Left My Phone at Home
titleZh: 我把手机忘在家里的那一天
passage:
Last Friday, I left my phone at home. I only found it when I was on the bus. At first, I felt very worried. My friends often send messages on WeChat. I did not want to miss anything. But I could not go back. So I just went to school.

In the morning, I kept thinking about my phone. During the break, I saw my classmates looking at their phones. Some were taking photos. Some were playing games. I felt a little lonely. Then my best friend Lily came to me. She said, "Let's go to the library. You can borrow a book." We read together and talked about the story. I felt much better.

In the afternoon, we had a PE class. We played basketball. I ran and jumped. I did not think about my phone at all. I felt happy and free.

After school, I got home and found my phone. There were many messages. But I did not read them right away. I found that I could live without my phone for a day. It was not so bad. In fact, it was a good day.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The writer had a good day without his phone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The writer's friends sent him many messages.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 文章讲述了作者一天没带手机，最后发现没有手机也可以过得很好。B项概括了全文主旨。A项错误，手机是忘在家里，不是丢在公交车上。C项是文中的细节，不是主旨。D项只是下午的一个活动，不能概括全文。

title: The School That Runs on Sunshine
titleZh: 阳光驱动的学校
passage:
In many cities, schools use a lot of electricity every day. Lights, computers and air conditioners all need power. Most of this power comes from coal. Burning coal is bad for the air. It also makes the Earth warmer.

Last year, a middle school in Nanjing tried something new. Workers put solar panels on the roof of the teaching building. These panels turn sunlight into electricity. Now the school uses the sun to power its lights and computers. On sunny days, the school even has extra power. It gives the extra power to nearby homes for free.

"At first, we thought it was too good to be true," says Mr. Li, a science teacher. "But it really works. Our electricity bill is much smaller now." Students also learn a lot from the panels. They watch the meters and write down how much power the sun makes each day. Some students even start to turn off lights when they leave a room.

Solar power is clean and never runs out. Of course, it does not work well at night or on rainy days. But for many schools, it is a bright idea. It saves money and helps the Earth at the same time.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coal is the best way to make electricity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A school uses solar power to save energy and money.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students in Nanjing do not like science classes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Air conditioners use too much power in summer.

questions.explanation: 文章主要讲述南京一所中学在楼顶安装太阳能板，用太阳能发电，节省电费并帮助地球。B项概括准确。A项与文章相反，文章说烧煤污染空气；C项文中未提学生不喜欢科学课；D项只是文中提到的一个细节，不是主旨。

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 文中明确提到“It gives the extra power to nearby homes for free.”，故选C。A、B、D项文中均未提及，属于无中生有。

questions.question: What can we infer about the students from the last two paragraphs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They become more careful about using electricity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They want to become solar panel workers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They stop using computers at school.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They think solar power is useless at night.

questions.explanation: 文中说学生记录太阳能发电量，有的还主动关灯，可以推断他们更注意节约用电，故选A。B项文中没有依据；C项与文章相反，学校仍使用电脑；D项是常识，不是从学生行为推断出来的。

questions.question: The underlined word "extra" in Paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.

choices.text: more than needed

choices.label: B
choices.text: very expensive

choices.label: C

title: The Boy Who Found a Hidden History
titleZh: 发现隐藏历史的男孩
passage:
Last summer, Jack, a 13-year-old boy, was walking in the hills near his home. He often went there to look for interesting stones. That day, he saw something shiny under a bush. He picked it up and found it was a small metal coin. It looked very old and had strange marks on it.

Jack took the coin home and showed it to his father. His father said, "This might be from an old town. We should tell the museum." The next day, they went to the town museum. A scientist looked at the coin carefully. She said, "This coin is over 800 years old. It can tell us about the people who lived here long ago."

The museum sent a team to the hills. They found more coins and old walls. It was an old market place. People bought and sold things there 800 years ago. Jack felt very happy. He said, "I just wanted to find a nice stone, but I found a piece of history!"

Now, Jack helps the museum on weekends. He learns about the past and shares it with his friends. He hopes one day he can become an archaeologist.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How to become an archaeologist.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A boy's discovery of an old coin and its importance.

title: Learning Chinese with Grandma
titleZh: 和奶奶一起学中文
passage:
Lily is a middle school student. She lives in Canada. Her parents come from China, but Lily speaks only English at school. She wants to learn Chinese.

Last summer, Lily's grandma came to visit. Grandma could not speak English. Lily could not speak much Chinese. At first, they smiled and used hand signs. It was fun but hard.

Lily had an idea. She put a small word card on the fridge. The card said "ni hao". Every morning, she read it with Grandma. Then she put more cards on the table, the door, and the TV. Each card had one Chinese word. Grandma pointed at the card and said the word slowly. Lily listened and repeated.

At dinner, Lily tried to say "I am hungry" in Chinese. Grandma laughed and gave her a big bowl of noodles. Lily felt happy. She learned eight new words that week.

Now Lily still learns Chinese with cards. She also calls Grandma every Sunday. "Chinese is not easy," Lily says. "But it is fun. And I can talk to my grandma!"

title: The School Music Club
titleZh: 学校音乐俱乐部
passage:
The school music club started three years ago. At first, only five students joined it. They met in a small room and played simple songs. The teacher, Mr. Li, was very kind. He said, "Music can make us happy. Let's share it with others."

Last year, the club grew bigger. Now about thirty students are in it. They have different hobbies. Some like singing, and some like playing the piano or the guitar. They practice every Tuesday and Friday after school. Sometimes they practice for two hours. It is hard work, but they enjoy it.

Next month, the club will give a show for all the students and teachers. They will sing songs and play music. Liu Mei, a club member, says, "I was shy before. But now I can sing in front of many people. Music gives me courage."

Mr. Li is proud of his students. He says, "The show is not just about music. It is about teamwork and friendship. When we work together, we can do great things."

The club is like a big family. Everyone helps each other. If you love music, you can join them. They will welcome you with a smile.

title: The Bus Ride That Changed My View
titleZh: 改变我看法的一次公交之旅
passage:
Every morning, I take the bus to school. The ride takes about twenty minutes. Usually, I sit by the window and listen to music. But one day, something different happened.

A little girl got on the bus with her grandmother. The girl was crying. She had lost her bus card. The driver saw her and said, "Don't worry. You can ride for free today." The girl stopped crying and smiled. She said, "Thank you, sir!"

Then an old man stood up and gave his seat to the grandmother. "Please sit here," he said. The grandmother thanked him. Other people on the bus also smiled. I saw a young man help a woman with her heavy bags. I also saw a boy give his candy to the little girl.

I always thought the bus was just a way to go from one place to another. But that day, I learned it is more than that. It is a small world where people help each other. Now I look forward to my bus ride every day. I even say hello to the driver and other passengers. A simple bus ride can make my day happy.

title: The Little Garden Helper
titleZh: 小花园帮手
passage:
Every Saturday morning, Lily goes to the community garden. She is only twelve, but she is a volunteer. She helps old people take care of the plants.

Last month, the garden was in a mess. Weeds were everywhere, and the flowers looked sad. An old man named Mr. Chen said, "We need young hands." Lily read the notice on the school board and decided to join. Her parents were happy and bought her a small pair of gloves.

At first, Lily didn't know what to do. She pulled out the wrong plants. But Mr. Chen was patient. He taught her how to tell weeds from vegetables. "This is a tomato plant," he said. "It will give us red fruit in summer."

Now Lily can do many things. She waters the flowers, picks up litter, and writes down when each plant needs care. She also brings her friends to help. "It's like a big family," she says. "I learn a lot, and I feel happy."

Mr. Chen says Lily is a great helper. The garden is clean and green again. More children come every week. Lily smiles, "Small hands can make a big difference."

title: The Little Money Jar

passage:
Li Ming is a middle school student. He gets 20 yuan from his parents every week. In the past, he spent all the money on snacks and small toys. He never had money left at the end of the week.

One day, his teacher talked about saving money in class. "If you save a little every week, you can buy something big later," she said. Li Ming thought about it. He wanted a new basketball, but it cost 120 yuan. His parents said he had to buy it with his own money.

So Li Ming got a glass jar. He wrote "Basketball" on it. Every Monday, he put 10 yuan into the jar. He only spent the other 10 yuan. At first, it was hard. He wanted to buy ice cream and storybooks. But he kept saving.

After twelve weeks, Li Ming opened the jar. He counted the money: 120 yuan! He was very happy. He bought the basketball and played with his friends. Now he saves money every week. He says, "Saving is not easy, but it feels great!"

title: The Rise of Vertical Farming: Growing Up, Not Out
titleZh: 垂直农业的兴起：向上生长，而非向外扩张
passage:
By 2050, the world's population is expected to reach nearly 10 billion, and feeding everyone will require about 70% more food than we produce today. Yet the land available for farming is shrinking, while climate change brings more droughts and floods. How can we grow more food with less land? One promising answer is vertical farming.

Instead of spreading crops across fields, vertical farms grow them in stacked layers inside buildings, often in cities. Plants are raised without soil, using nutrient-rich water, and are lit by LED lamps that mimic sunlight. Because the environment is controlled, temperature, humidity and light can be adjusted to suit each crop, so plants grow faster and are harvested all year round. Some vertical farms produce ten times the yield of a traditional field of the same size.

Supporters point out that vertical farms use up to 95% less water, since the water is recycled, and they need no pesticides because pests rarely enter the sealed buildings. What's more, because the farms are located in cities, vegetables can be delivered fresh to supermarkets within hours, cutting down on transport and carbon emissions.

However, critics argue that vertical farming is far from a perfect solution. It consumes huge amounts of electricity, and if that power comes from coal, the environmental benefits are questionable. Building and running such farms is also expensive, which means their products often cost more than ordinary vegetables. For now, vertical farms mostly grow leafy greens and herbs; staple crops like wheat and rice remain too costly to produce this way.

Perhaps vertical farming will not replace traditional agriculture. But as a supplement, it may help cities become more self-sufficient and reduce the pressure on our planet's limited farmland. The technology is still young, and its future will depend on cheaper, cleaner energy.

title: The Quiet Power of Repair Cafés
titleZh: 修理咖啡馆的静默力量
passage:
In a world where new smartphones are released every year and broken appliances are often thrown away, a quiet movement is growing. Repair cafés—community gatherings where people bring broken items and volunteers help fix them—are spreading across Europe, North America, and Asia. The idea is simple: instead of buying new things, we should repair what we already have. This not only saves money but also reduces waste, which is a major environmental problem.

The first repair café was opened in Amsterdam in 2009 by Martine Postma, a former journalist. She was tired of seeing perfectly good items being discarded. Today, there are more than 2,000 repair cafés worldwide. At these events, volunteers with skills in electronics, sewing, and bicycle repair offer their time for free. Visitors bring anything from toasters to trousers. About 70% of items are successfully repaired.

Why does this matter for the environment? According to the United Nations, electronic waste is now the fastest-growing waste stream in the world. In 2019, the world produced 53.6 million metric tons of e-waste, but only 17% was properly recycled. The rest ended up in landfills, where toxic chemicals can leak into soil and water. Repair cafés directly reduce this waste by extending the life of products. They also teach people how to fix things, which builds a culture of repair rather than replacement.

However, repair cafés face challenges. Many modern devices are designed to be difficult to repair, with glued components and special screws. Some manufacturers even prevent independent repair by limiting access to parts and manuals. In response, the "right to repair" movement is pushing for laws that require companies to make their products more repairable. The European Union has already passed rules requiring manufacturers to provide spare parts for up to 10 years for certain appliances.

Repair cafés may not solve the entire waste crisis, but they represent a shift in thinking. As Postma says, "We don't just fix things; we fix the way people think about their belongings." In a consumer society, that may be the most important repair of all.

title: Walking: The Simple Secret to Better Health
titleZh: 步行：改善健康的简单秘诀
passage:
In our fast-paced world, many people believe that getting fit requires intense workouts or expensive gym memberships. However, a growing body of research suggests that one of the most effective forms of exercise is also one of the simplest: walking.

According to a study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association, adults who walked at least 7,000 steps a day had a 50% to 70% lower risk of dying from all causes compared to those who walked fewer than 7,000 steps. The benefits were consistent across different age groups and health conditions. What's more, the study found that walking speed mattered less than the total number of steps.

Walking offers numerous advantages beyond longevity. It is low-impact, meaning it puts less stress on joints than running, making it suitable for people of all ages. It requires no special equipment other than a pair of comfortable shoes. It can be done almost anywhere—in a park, around the neighborhood, or even inside a shopping mall. Moreover, walking can be easily integrated into daily routines. You can walk to work, take the stairs instead of the elevator, or walk during lunch breaks.

Despite these benefits, many people still struggle to walk regularly. One reason is that modern life encourages sedentary habits. We sit at desks, drive cars, and spend hours in front of screens. Another reason is psychological: some people think walking is not "real" exercise. They believe that unless they are sweating heavily or feeling exhausted, they are not doing enough.

Experts suggest starting small. A 10-minute walk after dinner can be a good beginning. Over time, you can gradually increase the duration and frequency. The key is consistency, not intensity. As Dr. Smith, a public health researcher, puts it, "The best exercise is the one you will actually do. And for most people, that is walking."

title: The Power of Productive Struggle in Learning
titleZh: 有效挣扎在学习中的力量
topic: 教育方式——提倡让学生经历“有效挣扎”而非直接给答案
passage:
In many classrooms, a familiar scene unfolds: a student stares at a math problem, puzzled. Within seconds, the teacher rushes over and provides the solution. While this may seem helpful, a growing number of educators argue that such immediate rescue actually harms learning. They advocate for what is called "productive struggle"—allowing students to grapple with challenging tasks without instant assistance.

Productive struggle is grounded in the idea that learning is not a spectator sport. When students wrestle with a problem, their brains work harder to make connections, leading to deeper understanding. A study by Manu Kapur at ETH Zurich found that students who struggled with a problem before receiving instruction outperformed those who were taught the conventional way. The struggle, it seems, primes the brain for learning.

However, productive struggle does not mean leaving students to flounder endlessly. The key is to provide appropriate support—what psychologists call "scaffolding." Teachers might offer hints, ask probing questions, or break the task into smaller steps. The goal is to keep students in what Lev Vygotsky termed the "zone of proximal development," where a task is challenging but achievable with guidance.

Critics worry that struggle may frustrate students and damage their confidence. But proponents counter that overcoming obstacles builds resilience and a growth mindset. When students finally solve a problem on their own, the sense of accomplishment is far greater than if they had been given the answer. As the saying goes, "Smooth seas do not make skillful sailors."

In an age when answers are just a click away, teaching students to embrace struggle may be one of the most valuable lessons we can offer. It prepares them not just for tests, but for life's inevitable challenges.

title: When AI Becomes a Classmate
titleZh: 当AI成为同学
topic: 人工智能在教育中的应用
passage:
Imagine a classroom where every student has a personal tutor who never gets tired, never loses patience, and can explain a difficult math problem in five different ways. This is not a scene from a science fiction movie. In many schools around the world, artificial intelligence, or AI, is already playing the role of a teaching assistant.

AI-powered learning apps can analyze how a student solves problems. If a learner repeatedly makes mistakes with fractions, the system notices the pattern and provides extra practice. Unlike a human teacher who must divide attention among forty students, an AI tutor can focus on one learner at a time, adjusting the speed and difficulty level to match individual needs. Supporters argue that this personalized approach could help slower students catch up while allowing faster ones to move ahead.

However, critics warn that relying too much on AI may weaken the human connection that lies at the heart of education. A machine can check grammar and correct equations, but it cannot sense a student's frustration or offer a word of encouragement when confidence is low. Moreover, AI systems are only as good as the data they are trained on. If the data contains bias, the lessons may unfairly favor certain groups of students.

Perhaps the wisest path forward is not to choose between AI and human teachers, but to combine their strengths. AI can handle repetitive tasks and provide instant feedback, freeing teachers to focus on creative activities, class discussions, and emotional support. In this partnership, technology serves as a tool, not a replacement. The goal is not to build a classroom without teachers, but to create one where every student feels seen, challenged, and supported—whether the help comes from a human or a machine.

title: The Hidden Language of Honeybee Dances
titleZh: 蜜蜂舞蹈中的隐藏语言
passage:
When a honeybee discovers a rich source of nectar, it does not simply fly back to the hive and expect others to follow. Instead, it performs a remarkable behavior known as the "waggle dance," a figure-eight movement that communicates the direction and distance of the food to its hive mates. This discovery, made by Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch in the 1940s, earned him a Nobel Prize and changed our understanding of animal communication.

The dance contains precise information. The angle of the bee's body relative to the vertical comb indicates the direction of the food in relation to the sun. If the food is directly toward the sun, the bee dances straight upward. If it is 60 degrees to the left of the sun, the bee angles its body 60 degrees to the left of vertical. The duration of the waggle portion signals distance: roughly one second of waggling corresponds to about one kilometer. Thus, hive mates can locate food sources without ever having seen them.

However, recent research suggests that the dance is not a perfect map. Scientists at Virginia Tech found that bees adjust their dances based on the hive's physical condition. When the comb is tilted or uneven, the dancers modify their angles, and the followers interpret these modified dances correctly. This means the communication system is more flexible than previously thought.

Moreover, the dance may serve purposes beyond giving directions. Some studies indicate that the dance also motivates other bees to leave the hive and forage, and it may even help regulate the colony's division of labor. Young bees that follow dances tend to start foraging earlier than those that do not.

Understanding bee communication has practical value. Farmers can use this knowledge to improve pollination strategies, and engineers have designed robots that mimic bee dances to guide real bees to specific crops. As we continue to study these tiny dancers, we uncover not only the secrets of the hive but also lessons about cooperation and adaptation that resonate far beyond the world of insects.

title: The Quiet Value of Space Exploration
titleZh: 太空探索的无声价值
topic: 太空探索的意义与价值
passage:
When a rocket lifts off, most people watch the fire and smoke. But the real story of space exploration is often quieter. It is the story of technologies developed for missions that later improve life on Earth.

Consider the challenge of keeping astronauts safe in space. Engineers must design systems that work perfectly without repair. To meet this demand, they created lightweight materials, better batteries, and advanced water purification. These innovations did not stay in space. Today, they are used in hospitals, homes, and industries. The camera in your phone, for example, evolved from technology first made for space probes.

Space exploration also changes how we see ourselves. When astronauts describe the Earth as a small blue ball in endless darkness, their words remind us that our planet is fragile. This perspective has led to stricter environmental policies and greater international cooperation. In 1987, the Montreal Protocol, which aimed to protect the ozone layer, was signed partly because satellite images showed the damage clearly. Without space technology, such global agreements would be much harder to reach.

Critics argue that we should solve problems on Earth first. It is a fair point. However, history suggests that space research and earthly needs are not competitors. The Apollo program, for instance, cost billions but returned many times that amount through new industries and jobs. Moreover, the challenges of space demand teamwork that crosses borders, setting an example for solving other global issues.

Space exploration is not just about escaping Earth. It is about improving it. The next time you see a rocket launch, remember: the greatest benefits may not be on the moon, but right here at home.

title: The Slow Food Movement: A Recipe for Change
titleZh: 慢食运动：变革的良方
passage:
In a world where fast food chains dominate and meals are often eaten on the go, the Slow Food movement offers a different recipe for life. Founded in Italy in 1986 by Carlo Petrini, the movement began as a protest against the opening of a McDonald's near the Spanish Steps in Rome. Today, it has grown into a global organization with supporters in over 160 countries.

Slow Food is not just about eating slowly. It is a philosophy that connects the pleasure of food with a commitment to community and the environment. The movement encourages people to buy locally produced food, to cook at home, and to enjoy meals with family and friends. By doing so, it aims to preserve traditional cooking methods and local food cultures that are at risk of disappearing.

One of the key ideas of Slow Food is "eco-gastronomy," which recognizes the strong link between our food choices and the health of the planet. Supporters argue that industrial farming, while efficient, often harms the environment through the overuse of chemicals and the loss of biodiversity. They believe that choosing seasonal, organic, and local foods can reduce our carbon footprint and support small farmers.

Critics, however, point out that Slow Food can be expensive and time-consuming, making it inaccessible to many people. They argue that for low-income families, fast food is often the only affordable option. In response, Slow Food supporters emphasize that the movement also promotes food education and community gardens, which can make healthy eating more accessible.

Despite the criticism, the Slow Food movement has inspired countless individuals and communities to rethink their relationship with food. It reminds us that every meal is an opportunity to make a choice—one that affects not only our health but also the world around us.

title: The Silent Language of City Streets
titleZh: 城市街道的无声语言
passage:
Walk down any busy city street and you will notice them: benches placed at just the right angle, trees that shade a crossing, a fountain that masks the noise of traffic. These are not accidents. They are the work of urban designers who understand that a city's health depends on something far less visible than skyscrapers—its social life.

For decades, city planners focused on efficiency. Roads were widened, sidewalks were narrowed, and public spaces were treated as leftover land. The result was predictable: neighborhoods that functioned well on maps but felt cold on foot. People hurried through them without stopping, and strangers rarely spoke.

A growing number of researchers argue that this approach missed something essential. In a famous study of a Philadelphia neighborhood, sociologist Ray Oldenburg observed that casual, repeated encounters—a nod to a neighbor, a brief chat at a bus stop—build trust and a sense of belonging. He called these informal gathering places "third places," distinct from home and work. Without them, he warned, communities weaken.

Some cities have taken this idea seriously. In Barcelona, "superblocks" close certain streets to cars, turning intersections into small plazas where children play and elderly residents sit. In Singapore, housing estates are designed with covered walkways and shared gardens that encourage residents to meet. These changes are not merely aesthetic. Studies suggest they can reduce loneliness and even improve physical health.

Critics point out that such projects can raise property values and push out the very people they aim to help. That is a fair concern. Yet the core insight remains: a city is not a machine for moving people; it is a stage for living together. The next time you rest on a bench and strike up a conversation with a stranger, remember that someone designed that moment—or at least made it possible.

title: The Brush That Paints China's Soul
titleZh: 描绘中国灵魂的毛笔
passage:
In an age when typing on screens has become second nature, few young people stop to consider the humble writing brush that once shaped Chinese civilization. Yet this simple tool, made of animal hair and bamboo, carries within its strands a philosophy that has endured for thousands of years.

Chinese calligraphy is far more than a means of recording words. It is a visual art that demands the perfect balance of body and mind. When a calligrapher picks up the brush, every stroke must be delivered with controlled energy. A single character may take years to master, for its beauty lies not only in the shape but also in the rhythm and spirit expressed through each line. As an old saying goes, "The brush is an extension of the heart."

Unlike many Western art forms that encourage individual expression, traditional calligraphy values inheritance. Learners begin by copying the works of ancient masters, absorbing the rules of structure and movement before developing their own style. This process teaches patience and respect—qualities that modern society often overlooks. In a world obsessed with speed, calligraphy reminds us that true excellence grows slowly.

Today, calligraphy is experiencing a quiet revival. Schools across China have reintroduced it into the curriculum, and online platforms offer virtual lessons to anyone curious about this ancient craft. Some young artists are even combining calligraphy with digital design, proving that tradition and innovation can coexist. The brush, it seems, refuses to be forgotten.

So the next time you admire a piece of Chinese calligraphy, remember: it is not merely ink on paper. It is a dialogue between the past and the present, a dance of the hand guided by the heart.
